final_report.summary: Successfully implemented an activity-aware adaptive handoff monitor that replaces the rigid 55-minute timeout with intelligent filesystem-based activity detection. The core problem was that AtlasForge's fixed timeout would kill long-running TESTING sessions even when the LLM was actively working, causing cascading failures after 3 timeouts. The solution monitors workspace file modifications every 30 seconds and only triggers a handoff after sustained inactivity (15 minutes with no file changes), with stage-aware base timeouts (TESTING gets 4 hours, BUILDING gets 2 hours, others keep 55 minutes). The implementation is fully model-agnostic — it watches the filesystem, not LLM output — so it works identically with Claude, Codex, Gemini, or any other provider. All 83 tests pass including 28 adversarial tests designed to break the system.
key_achievements: Built ActivityAwareHandoffMonitor (~290 lines) that detects real filesystem activity instead of using wall-clock time
Stage-aware timeout configuration: TESTING=240min, BUILDING=120min, default=55min, absolute max=360min
Model-agnostic design — monitors file mtimes only, zero LLM-specific dependencies
Full backward compatibility — falls back to TimeBasedHandoffMonitor when no stage is provided
Environment variable overrides for all timeout constants (AF_TESTING_TIMEOUT_MINUTES, AF_INACTIVITY_THRESHOLD_MINUTES, etc.)
83/83 tests passing including adversarial tests for race conditions and boundary cases
Integrated into atlasforge_conductor.py with stage passthrough and adaptive subprocess timeouts
challenges_overcome: Designing activity detection that is truly model-agnostic (filesystem watching vs. output parsing)
Balancing safety (detecting genuinely hung sessions) with flexibility (allowing legitimate long runs)
Three-tier handoff trigger system: absolute max, inactivity-after-base-timeout, and extended-inactivity
Maintaining backward compatibility so non-stage-aware callers get original 55-minute behavior
Ensuring the subprocess timeout in conductor matches the stage-aware timeout to prevent premature kills
lessons_learned: Filesystem activity (mtime monitoring) is the most reliable model-agnostic liveness signal — it works regardless of LLM provider
Fixed timeouts are fundamentally wrong for variable-duration stages; activity-based detection is strictly superior
The three-timeout-out shutdown logic was the real culprit — it treated expected long runs as errors
Stage-aware configuration is essential: different R&D stages have fundamentally different timing profiles
Environment variable overrides are critical for tuning without code changes in production
